label: PART II
title: Recognizing Design Friction
lead: Treat smells as evidence about change cost, not as automatic violations.

chapters.title: Bloaters
chapters.intro: Bloaters grow until the reader can no longer hold the relevant idea in working memory.

concepts.title: Long Method
concepts.definition: A Long Method asks the reader to hold several phases, abstraction levels, or clusters of local state in mind at once. Line count is only a rough signal; mixed intent is the real smell.
concepts.look_for: Look for comment-separated phases, deeply nested branches, variables used by only one phase, and changes that repeatedly touch different regions of the same method.
concepts.walkthrough: The before version makes `BuildInvoiceSummary` own arithmetic, regional tax selection, and text formatting. A reader must track `subtotal`, `tax`, and `total` while moving between three different levels of intent. In the after version, the method coordinates `CalculateSubtotal`, `AddTax`, and `FormatSummary`; each name exposes a phase and creates a place for its local details. The observable summary should remain identical, making Extract Method the natural refactoring. The smell is not established by a particular line count. A fifty-line parser with one cohesive algorithm may be easier to follow than a twelve-line method that mixes persistence, authorization, and formatting. The change pressure makes the diagnosis useful: a tax-rule change should not require navigating through invoice presentation, and a formatting change should not risk arithmetic. Python shows the same separation through named functions.
concepts.caution: Do not extract tiny fragments whose names merely paraphrase their statements. Extract a coherent decision, calculation, or phase that improves the caller's story.
concepts.related: Related: Extract Method; Replace Method with Method Object

concepts.title: Large Class
concepts.definition: A Large Class owns too many responsibilities, collaborators, or independent reasons to change. Field and method clusters often reveal smaller concepts trapped inside it.
concepts.look_for: Group members by the data they use and the stakeholders that change them. Extract a collaborator when one cluster has its own vocabulary and lifecycle.
concepts.walkthrough: `InvoiceManager` is suspect because pricing and email delivery change for unrelated reasons and use different collaborators. Extracting `InvoiceCalculator` and `InvoiceMailer` gives each cluster a name and owner. The number of lines is secondary: even a short class can be 'large' in responsibility if every change belongs to a different business concern. Conversely, a facade may expose many operations while delegating them to cohesive components and remain a useful boundary. The after version lets finance-related tests target `CalculateTotal` without SMTP setup and lets delivery changes avoid pricing code. Python establishes the same split. This smell often manifests as several groups of fields that never appear together, a constructor with many unrelated services, or merge conflicts from independent teams editing the same file. Extract Class is the shown remedy, but the diagnosis should begin with change history and responsibility rather than a numerical size threshold.
concepts.caution: A broad facade or application coordinator can be intentional. Judge whether the class owns mixed policy, not whether it has many methods or delegates to focused collaborators.
concepts.related: Related: Extract Class; Single Responsibility Principle; Divergent Change

concepts.title: Primitive Obsession
concepts.definition: Primitive Obsession represents a domain concept with an undifferentiated string, number, or boolean even though the value has rules, units, formatting, or identity of its own.
concepts.look_for: Look for repeated validation, formatting, unit conversion, or accidentally interchangeable arguments surrounding the same primitive value.
concepts.walkthrough: In the before signature, `customerEmail` is only a `string`; the compiler cannot distinguish it from `body` or any other text, and every caller can pass an unvalidated value. `EmailAddress` gives the concept a name and centralizes its minimum invariant. Once an instance exists, `SendReceipt` can rely on that construction rule instead of repeating validation. A production email parser would need stronger rules than `Contains('@')`; the small check is here to show ownership, not to define the internet standard. Python's class provides the same runtime boundary, while its type annotation can help static tools. This value-object move becomes especially valuable for money, dates, identifiers, units, and security-sensitive tokens. Primitive Obsession is not a demand to wrap every scalar. A local loop counter is correctly an integer; a `CustomerId` may deserve its own type because confusing it with an `OrderId` causes real defects.
concepts.caution: Do not create ceremonial wrappers that add neither validation, meaning, nor type safety. Introduce a value type when the domain concept has durable behavior or prevents plausible mistakes.
concepts.related: Related: Replace Data Value with Object; Value Object; Type safety

concepts.title: Long Parameter List
concepts.definition: A Long Parameter List makes callers supply many separate values, often in an order that is hard to verify. Repeated groups can reveal a missing domain object or an object exposing too much internal need.
concepts.look_for: Look for recurring argument groups, adjacent values of the same type, several booleans, and call sites that require comments to explain positions.
concepts.walkthrough: The original `CreateQuote` call exposes five independent positions. `street` and `postalCode` travel together as an address, while destination, speed, and insurance form the shipping choice. `Address` and `ShippingOptions` name those concepts and make a call harder to scramble. They also create homes for validation and future behavior such as zone lookup. The quote algorithm is intentionally omitted in both versions because the refactoring should preserve it; the teaching point is the signature and ownership of related values. Python callers could mitigate positional ambiguity with keyword arguments, but keywords do not centralize the relationship or validation. A parameter object is justified when the group recurs or has domain meaning. If unrelated inputs are stuffed into a generic `Options` bag merely to reduce the visible count, the API has become less honest rather than more cohesive.
concepts.caution: Do not hide unrelated arguments inside a junk-drawer options object. The new object should represent a real concept with a coherent reason to change.
concepts.related: Related: Introduce Parameter Object; Preserve Whole Object; Data Clumps

concepts.title: Data Clumps
concepts.definition: Data Clumps are small groups of values that repeatedly appear together in fields, parameters, or locals. Their persistent companionship suggests an unnamed concept.
concepts.look_for: Notice coordinates, date ranges, credentials, and address parts repeated across APIs. Remove one member mentally: if the remainder loses meaning, the values likely belong together.
concepts.walkthrough: The before signature contains two pairs that must stay aligned: `fromLatitude` with `fromLongitude`, and `toLatitude` with `toLongitude`. Passing four doubles makes it easy to swap values, and every consuming API must rediscover the pairing. `Coordinates` turns each pair into one value with a name. `Distance` now communicates that it operates between two points, and coordinate validation or formatting has an obvious owner. The distance formula remains the same, so introducing the value object is a structural change. Python type annotations make the intended pair visible to readers and tools, although runtime enforcement depends on the class. A clump is stronger evidence when it recurs across several signatures or field sets. Grouping arbitrary values simply because they appear in one call does not reveal a concept; it creates a bag.
concepts.caution: Do not group unrelated values solely to shorten a parameter list. The extracted value should have cohesive meaning and preferably its own invariant or behavior.
concepts.related: Related: Extract Class; Introduce Parameter Object; Primitive Obsession

chapters.title: Object-oriented abusers
chapters.intro: These smells use inheritance, fields, or polymorphism in ways that obscure rather than clarify the model.

concepts.title: Switch Statements
concepts.definition: The Switch Statements smell is repeated branching on the same type code across several operations. One local switch can be clear; parallel switches make every new case a scattered change.
concepts.look_for: Search for the same enum or discriminator in pricing, rendering, validation, and delivery code. If adding one variant touches all of them, centralize that variation.
concepts.walkthrough: The original `ShippingFee` branch is not objectionable by itself. It becomes evidence of this smell if `CustomerType` drives similar branches throughout discounts, support priority, and returns. Then adding a new customer type requires synchronized edits across the codebase. The after version moves the fee decision into `IShippingPolicy` implementations, so each policy owns its behavior and callers invoke `Fee` without inspecting a type code. Replace Conditional with Polymorphism is the refactoring; Strategy is one possible resulting role. Python uses compatible objects without a formal interface. For a closed, stable set of cases, a switch or pattern match may remain the clearest form, especially when all alternatives belong in one function. The diagnostic target is scattered variation, not the syntax keyword `switch` or `if`.
concepts.caution: Do not replace every switch with subclasses. Pattern matching is often ideal for a closed set of data variants; refactor when the same axis of variation is scattered and keeps growing.
concepts.related: Related: Replace Conditional with Polymorphism; Strategy; Open/Closed Principle

concepts.title: Temporary Field
concepts.definition: A Temporary Field is stored on an object but valid only during one operation or phase. The object's state is therefore partly meaningful, and readers must remember when the field can be trusted.
concepts.look_for: Look for fields cleared after a method, initialized to placeholders, or checked for null only because one calculation uses them. Keep such working state local or give it a dedicated owner.
concepts.walkthrough: In the problematic design, `subtotal` and `tax` would be fields on `QuoteCalculator` even though they describe only one invocation of `Calculate`. Between calls they would be stale or meaningless, and concurrent calls could overwrite each other's working state. The revised method keeps both values local and returns a `Quote` that explicitly represents the durable result. The calculator itself remains valid at every point and becomes naturally reentrant. Python has the same distinction between instance attributes and function locals. If a calculation grows too complicated for locals, a short-lived method object can own the state and make its lifecycle explicit. A cache is different from a temporary field because it has an intentional reuse and invalidation contract; that contract should be named rather than confused with incidental working memory.
concepts.caution: Do not remove a legitimate cache or lifecycle field without understanding its contract. The smell is state whose validity is hidden or restricted to one temporary phase.
concepts.related: Related: Replace Method with Method Object; Extract Class; Mutable Shared State

concepts.title: Refused Bequest
concepts.definition: Refused Bequest appears when a subclass inherits operations or state it cannot meaningfully support. The hierarchy was chosen for reuse, but the subtype is not behaviorally substitutable.
concepts.look_for: Look for inherited methods that throw, do nothing, expose irrelevant state, or cause clients to exclude one subtype before calling the base contract.
concepts.walkthrough: A base `Bird` contract that includes `Fly` would force `Penguin` to inherit a promise it cannot keep. Throwing `NotSupportedException` only moves the dishonesty to runtime. Splitting `IBird` from `IFlyingBird` lets `Penguin` promise eating behavior and lets `Sparrow` promise both eating and flight. Clients that need flight request the narrower meaningful capability and no longer inspect concrete types. This directly connects Refused Bequest to the Liskov Substitution Principle: the symptom is unwanted inherited behavior; the deeper problem is a false substitution claim. Interface Segregation is also involved because implementers are no longer forced to support an irrelevant method. Python protocols document the same capability split without imposing nominal inheritance. When a subclass refuses only incidental implementation details but still honors the public meaning, the smell may not apply.
concepts.caution: Do not preserve a false hierarchy merely to reuse code. Extract the reusable implementation and compose it into types whose public contracts remain honest.
concepts.related: Related: Liskov Substitution Principle; Push Down Method; Replace Inheritance with Delegation

concepts.title: Alternative Classes with Different Interfaces
concepts.definition: Alternative Classes with Different Interfaces provide the same practical capability through incompatible names or call shapes, forcing clients to branch on which implementation they received.
concepts.look_for: When two components serve one role but clients call `Read` on one and `FetchText` on another, rename, adapt, or extract a common role after verifying their semantics truly match.
concepts.walkthrough: Both sources can provide text, but the legacy object calls its operation `FetchText` while the application expects `Read`. `LegacyTextSourceAdapter` translates that vocabulary and lets clients depend on one `ITextSource` role. No client needs a type check or vendor-specific method call. In C#, the interface makes the common contract nominal; Python can rely on both classes exposing `read`, optionally documented with a protocol. Adapter is useful when the legacy or third-party class cannot be renamed directly. If both classes belong to the application, Rename Method or Extract Interface may be simpler. Before unifying them, verify semantics such as encoding, caching, errors, and resource ownership. Two methods that both return strings may not actually make the same promise.
concepts.caution: Do not force a common interface based only on similar return types. Align names and shapes only after confirming that preconditions, results, errors, and side effects are substitutable.
concepts.related: Related: Adapter; Rename Method; Extract Interface

chapters.title: Change preventers
chapters.intro: These smells turn one conceptual change into several unrelated edits.

concepts.title: Divergent Change
concepts.definition: Divergent Change occurs when one module must be edited for several unrelated kinds of requirement. Different change axes converge on the same crowded owner.
concepts.look_for: Review change history and field usage. If formatting, persistence, authorization, and business rules repeatedly alter different regions of one class, separate those responsibilities.
concepts.walkthrough: The revised `ReportService` coordinates two collaborators but does not own their details. `IReportRepository` changes when storage changes; `IReportRenderer` changes when presentation changes. The service's own reason to change is the application workflow connecting them. In the problematic version, SQL and HTML lived in the same class, so unrelated requests repeatedly reopened it. That is divergent change: one class changes in different ways for different reasons. This is the mirror image of Shotgun Surgery, where one reason for change is scattered across many classes. Merely splitting code into technical layers is not automatically helpful; each extracted component should have coherent ownership and be independently understandable and testable. Python uses constructor-supplied collaborators to create the same boundary. Change history, not a single snapshot, provides the strongest evidence for this smell.
concepts.caution: Do not split by fashionable layer names without a real independent change pressure. Unnecessary separation can turn local work into cross-module navigation.
concepts.related: Related: Single Responsibility Principle; Extract Class; Shotgun Surgery

concepts.title: Shotgun Surgery
concepts.definition: Shotgun Surgery means one conceptual rule has no clear owner, so changing it requires small coordinated edits across many files or modules.
concepts.look_for: Search for repeated constants, formulas, conditions, error translations, and protocol details that always change together for one business request.
concepts.walkthrough: The tax rate and its regional condition previously appeared in several workflows. A rate change therefore required a search-and-edit campaign, and missing one copy produced inconsistent totals. `TaxPolicy.Calculate` gives that knowledge one owner; quoting and invoicing now ask the policy rather than knowing the formula. The number of files touched is not itself the smell - a cross-cutting feature may legitimately require broad work. Shotgun Surgery applies when those edits express one concept that ought to have a cohesive home. It is the inverse of Divergent Change: here one reason to change is scattered among many modules; there many reasons converge on one module. Python demonstrates the same centralization. The selected owner should remain small and domain-specific; moving every rule into a generic global service merely trades scattered knowledge for a god object.
concepts.caution: Centralization can create a new god service. Move the knowledge to the smallest cohesive policy, value object, or module that truly owns it.
concepts.related: Related: Move Method; Move Field; Divergent Change; DRY

concepts.title: Parallel Inheritance Hierarchies
concepts.definition: Parallel Inheritance Hierarchies arise when adding a subtype to one hierarchy forces a matching subtype in another. Two class trees encode the same axis of variation twice.
concepts.look_for: Notice paired names such as `DarkOrderScreen` and `DarkSettingsScreen`, followed by equivalent pairs for every new theme. Replace one dimension with composition.
concepts.walkthrough: The problematic design would create a screen hierarchy and then duplicate each screen subtype for every theme: order/dark, order/light, settings/dark, settings/light. Adding a theme forces a matching family of subclasses. In the revised design, `Screen` and `ITheme` represent independent dimensions. An order screen and settings screen can both receive the same `DarkTheme`; a new theme does not require new screen subclasses. Composition removes the lockstep between inheritance trees and prevents a combinatorial class count. Python achieves the same result by storing a theme collaborator. Two hierarchies are not problematic merely because both exist. The smell requires them to evolve in parallel because one variation was encoded twice. Bridge is a named pattern for separating an abstraction from an independently varying implementation, though ordinary composition may be all the vocabulary needed for a small case.
concepts.caution: Do not merge hierarchies that only happen to have similar names. The problem is forced lockstep evolution, not the presence of multiple independent taxonomies.
concepts.related: Related: Composition over inheritance; Bridge; Replace Inheritance with Delegation

chapters.title: Dispensables
chapters.intro: Dispensables add cognitive load without enough present value to justify it.

concepts.title: Comments
concepts.definition: Comments become a smell when they compensate for unclear naming, tangled flow, or missing domain vocabulary. Valuable comments preserve why, constraints, trade-offs, or surprising external facts.
concepts.look_for: When a comment narrates what the next lines do, try naming the operation or variable. Keep comments that explain information the code cannot express.
concepts.walkthrough: The before comment merely paraphrases the conditional, so it can drift when the threshold or international rule changes. `QualifiesForFreeShipping` turns that intent into an executable name and gives the policy a place to evolve. `meetsMinimum` makes the remaining numeric test readable without narrating syntax. This does not mean comments are bad. A note such as 'carrier contract requires dimensional weight rounded upward' preserves rationale and an external constraint that no method name can fully encode. API documentation, security assumptions, units, and carefully scoped workarounds can be essential. Treat the smell as a prompt: if code needs a paragraph to explain what it does, improve the code first; if future maintainers need to know why an odd but necessary choice exists, write the comment. Python follows the same replacement of narration with domain vocabulary.
concepts.caution: Do not delete rationale, regulatory context, units, or external-workaround details simply because comments appear in a smell catalog. Preserve knowledge the code cannot state.
concepts.related: Related: Extract Method; Rename Method; Documentation debt

concepts.title: Duplicate Code
concepts.definition: Duplicate Code repeats the same knowledge or algorithm in more than one place, allowing fixes and rule changes to drift between copies.
concepts.look_for: Confirm that the copies represent one rule and change for the same reason. Then give that rule one well-named owner.
concepts.python_expanded:
# Before: quoting and invoicing each copied the weight thresholds.
def calculate_shipping(weight):
    if weight <= 5:
        return 8
    return 12


quote_fee = calculate_shipping(order.weight)
invoice_fee = calculate_shipping(order.weight)
concepts.walkthrough: The shipping threshold and fees are business knowledge. If quoting and invoicing each implement `weight <= 5` with the same prices, a later rate change can update one copy and leave the other behind. `CalculateShipping` centralizes the rule, and both workflows ask it for the answer. Extract Method or Move Method might create that owner depending on the surrounding design. The important test is shared reason for change, not visual resemblance. Two loops that currently look alike may serve unrelated policies and deserve to diverge. Conversely, differently written expressions can duplicate the same rule. Python's callers use the same central function. A small amount of temporary duplication can be safer than prematurely inventing a common abstraction, especially while requirements are still revealing where the true boundary lies.
concepts.caution: A little duplication is often cheaper than the wrong abstraction. Consolidate after the shared meaning and change direction are clear, not merely because tokens match.
concepts.related: Related: DRY; Extract Method; Shotgun Surgery

concepts.title: Lazy Class
concepts.definition: A Lazy Class no longer earns the mental, naming, and navigation cost of existing. It often remains after responsibilities moved away or after speculative variation never arrived.
concepts.look_for: Look for classes that only forward one trivial operation, hold no invariant, mark no useful boundary, and have no independent reason to change.
concepts.walkthrough: `TotalCalculator` contributes no policy, validation, state, translation, or seam; `Calculate` merely renames the standard sum operation. Inlining it removes a class and method that every reader otherwise has to open. The behavior remains the sum of `invoice.Amounts`. This is a Lazy Class only because the abstraction has no present responsibility. A similarly small `TaxPolicy` could be valuable if it owns a volatile legal rule, and a one-method port can protect callers from an external vendor. Size is evidence, not the verdict. Examine change history, dependencies, and the concept's independent meaning. Python makes the needless wrapper particularly visible because the built-in `sum` is already expressive. Inline Class or Inline Method is the likely refactoring when callers do not need a migration boundary.
concepts.caution: Do not remove a small type that protects an invariant, marks an architectural boundary, or carries strong domain vocabulary. Small is not synonymous with lazy.
concepts.related: Related: Inline Class; Inline Method; Speculative Generality

concepts.title: Data Class
concepts.definition: A Data Class exposes state while outside code owns the rules that interpret or change it. Business behavior scatters and invariants become easy to bypass.
concepts.look_for: Notice services that repeatedly read several fields from the same entity to calculate answers or perform transitions. Move behavior to the owner when the rule belongs there.
concepts.walkthrough: Area depends entirely on `Rectangle.Width` and `Rectangle.Height`, so `CalculateArea` belongs naturally with those values. Callers no longer duplicate the formula or treat the rectangle as a passive bag. If validation such as positive dimensions matters, the same class can protect it at construction. This is the behavioral response to a Data Class smell. Not every data-centric type is a smell: DTOs, serialized messages, database projections, and UI view models are often intended to carry data across boundaries without domain behavior. The question is whether stable domain rules are living elsewhere only because the object exposes fields. Python's class demonstrates the same ownership. An immutable record can still be anemic if the domain expects transitions and rules; immutability and behavior ownership are separate concerns.
concepts.caution: Do not move orchestration, database access, or unrelated workflow into an entity merely to make it 'rich.' Transport shapes and messages are intentionally data-oriented.
concepts.related: Related: Anemic Domain Model; Move Method; Encapsulation

concepts.title: Dead Code
concepts.definition: Dead Code is unreachable, unused, obsolete, or permanently disabled behavior that continues to impose reading, testing, and maintenance cost.
concepts.look_for: Use compiler warnings, reference search, coverage, feature telemetry, and production evidence. Remove verified dead code and rely on version control for recovery.
concepts.walkthrough: `LegacyDiscount` represents an old 15-percent rule and has no callers. Keeping it beside `CurrentDiscount` forces readers to determine which policy is authoritative and leaves obsolete behavior available for accidental reuse. Removing the legacy method does not change runtime behavior precisely because nothing reaches it. Version control already preserves its history if investigation is needed later. Static reference search is strong evidence in ordinary code, but dynamic systems complicate the claim: reflection, dependency-injection scanning, serializers, templates, plug-ins, and external consumers may invoke code without a visible call. Python adds imports and name-based discovery to that list. Dead feature flags and commented-out blocks carry the same cognitive tax. Verify hidden entry points, delete confidently, and let tests and deployment evidence confirm the removal.
concepts.caution: Dynamic invocation and public APIs can hide usage. Verify reflection, serialization, plug-in registration, templates, and external consumers before deleting apparently unreferenced code.
concepts.related: Related: Inline Method; Feature flags; Code coverage

concepts.title: Speculative Generality
concepts.definition: Speculative Generality is flexibility built for hypothetical scenarios: unused interfaces, type parameters, hooks, layers, or configuration that every reader must understand but no caller needs.
concepts.look_for: Find abstractions with one implementation, parameters always passed the same value, and extension points with no current or committed consumer. Collapse them until a real second case appears.
concepts.python_expanded:
# Before: a generic receipt pipeline supported no other document type.
# After: the one real operation is direct.
def render_receipt(order):
    total = f"{order.total:.2f}"
    return f"Receipt {order.id}: {total}"


receipt = render_receipt(order)
concepts.walkthrough: The application currently renders one kind of receipt in one format. `RenderReceipt` states that need directly rather than requiring a generic document pipeline, renderer registry, unused type parameter, and configuration key for imagined formats. Removing those unused extension points lowers the cost of reading and changing the real behavior. If a PDF receipt or invoice format later arrives, the direct function can be refactored with concrete examples in hand. That is YAGNI applied as a smell diagnosis. A single interface implementation is not automatically speculative: an external payment port may still isolate genuine vendor volatility or protect the domain dependency direction. The evidence is whether the abstraction answers a real boundary or only a future story. Python's simple function makes the current requirement explicit and leaves ordinary refactoring available.
concepts.caution: Do not confuse prudent isolation of an external or irreversible dependency with speculation. A seam can be valuable before a second implementation when it controls real risk.
concepts.related: Related: YAGNI; Lazy Class; Inline Class; Remove Parameter

chapters.title: Couplers
chapters.intro: Couplers make one component know too much about another component's data, structure, or navigation path.

concepts.title: Feature Envy
concepts.definition: Feature Envy describes a method that chiefly interrogates another object's data to make a decision. The behavior may belong beside the data and invariants it interprets.
concepts.look_for: Count which object's fields a method reads. If most inputs come from one collaborator and form one domain rule, consider moving the method there.
concepts.walkthrough: The preference rule depends only on a customer's `lifetimeSpend`. When an outside pricing service repeatedly reads that field and compares it with `1_000`, it envies data owned by `Customer`. Moving the decision to `Customer.IsPreferred` puts the rule beside the value it interprets, hides the threshold, and lets callers ask a domain question. `discount` may still be calculated by a pricing policy because the actual discount amount could belong to a different responsibility. Feature Envy does not mean every method that uses another object should move. Application services legitimately coordinate several participants, and reporting code may intentionally read across a model. The strongest signal is concentrated use of one object's internals plus a rule that naturally describes that object. Python's underscore field and `is_preferred` method create the same ownership boundary.
concepts.caution: Do not force multi-object orchestration into whichever participant supplies the most fields. A coordinator is appropriate when no single object owns the whole decision.
concepts.related: Related: Move Method; Encapsulation; Tell, Don't Ask

concepts.title: Inappropriate Intimacy
concepts.definition: Inappropriate Intimacy occurs when classes rely on each other's internal representation or undocumented lifecycle details. Changes to private decisions repeatedly break the collaborator.
concepts.look_for: Look for direct collection mutation, friend-like access, knowledge of call ordering, and one class reaching through another to repair its state.
concepts.walkthrough: When callers can retrieve `lines` and mutate the collection, they must know how `Order` stores line items and which validations are required. `AddLine` replaces that intimate knowledge with a narrow operation and keeps the quantity invariant inside the owner. `CalculateTotal` also prevents consumers from depending on collection representation merely to ask an order question. The order can later change its internal storage without breaking callers. Interaction between classes is not itself intimacy; objects exist to collaborate. The smell appears when a collaborator depends on internal choices or lifecycle facts that should be private. C# access modifiers can enforce part of the boundary. Python relies more heavily on convention, but `_lines` plus behavior-bearing methods still communicates ownership. If two domain objects genuinely form one aggregate and protect a joint invariant, close collaboration may be intentional and should be documented as such.
concepts.caution: Closely collaborating domain objects are not automatically flawed. The smell is dependence on private decisions and hidden lifecycle facts, not ordinary message passing.
concepts.related: Related: Encapsulation; Hide Delegate; Move Method; Law of Demeter

concepts.title: Message Chains
concepts.definition: A Message Chain makes a caller navigate through several objects to obtain a result or trigger behavior. The caller becomes coupled to every link in the object graph.
concepts.look_for: Look for repeated forms such as `order.Customer.Address.Country.Code`. Ask the nearest owner for the business answer instead of exposing navigation to every caller.
concepts.walkthrough: The original caller knows that an order has a customer, the customer has a shipping address, the address has a country, and the country exposes `Code`. Any rearrangement of that graph leaks into every such caller. `Order.GetShippingCountryCode` gives the client a stable question and keeps navigation behind the owning boundary. Internally, `Order` delegates to `Customer`; the chain has moved to code responsible for that relationship. This refactoring is often called Hide Delegate. It should be selective. A short traversal over stable immutable data may be clearer than adding a forwarding method for every property. The smell is strongest when navigation is volatile, repeated, or used to perform behavior on a distant object. Python's leading underscore marks the customer reference as internal by convention and exposes the same domain-level query.
concepts.caution: Do not create a forwarding method for every possible path. Hide repeated or volatile navigation that callers should not own; leave simple stable data access direct.
concepts.related: Related: Hide Delegate; Law of Demeter; Middleman

concepts.title: Middleman
concepts.definition: A Middleman delegates nearly all of its public behavior without adding policy, translation, protection, lifecycle control, or a useful architectural seam.
concepts.look_for: Open forwarding methods and ask what the class contributes. If the answer is only another name and another file, let callers use the real capability.
concepts.walkthrough: `ReceiptFacade.SendAsync` accepts the same arguments, invokes `emailSender.SendAsync`, and returns the same task. It contributes no authorization, retry policy, address validation, format translation, or protection from a vendor API. Removing it shortens the dependency path and makes the real capability visible. That is Remove Middleman, and the externally observed send remains unchanged. Delegation alone does not establish the smell. A facade may intentionally provide a stable application vocabulary over a volatile subsystem; a proxy may enforce security or remote access; a port may preserve dependency direction. Those boundaries can be valuable even when their code is short. Judge what responsibility the layer owns rather than counting forwarding statements. Python's example shows the same absence of contribution without any async-specific implication.
concepts.caution: Keep a delegating facade, adapter, proxy, or port when the boundary itself protects callers or owns policy. Remove only forwarding that has no present responsibility.
concepts.related: Related: Remove Middleman; Inline Class; Facade; Proxy

chapters.title: Other original smell
chapters.intro: The original outline includes one library-boundary smell outside the main families.

concepts.title: Incomplete Library Class
concepts.definition: Incomplete Library Class describes a dependency type that almost serves the application but lacks a small operation, while the application cannot safely modify that library.
concepts.look_for: Add a focused extension, helper, or adapter in application vocabulary instead of forking the library or scattering the missing operation across callers.
concepts.walkthrough: `DateOnly` provides `DayOfWeek` but no application-level `IsWeekend` operation. The extension method adds that vocabulary without changing or subclassing the framework type. Callers share one definition instead of repeating Saturday/Sunday comparisons. Python uses a local function because monkey-patching the standard date type would create hidden global behavior. For a larger mismatch - different names, errors, or lifecycle - an Adapter would be more appropriate than many extensions. The smell is not a criticism of the library; no general library can predict every domain convenience. It identifies the pressure that can lead teams to copy missing behavior or fork a dependency. Keep the local addition narrow and owned by the application. If it starts recreating a substantial API, reconsider the dependency or build a deliberate wrapper.
concepts.caution: Do not grow a shadow standard library of loosely related extensions. Keep additions small, cohesive, discoverable, and tied to a real application need.
concepts.related: Related: Introduce Foreign Method; Introduce Local Extension; Adapter

chapters.title: Modern smells worth adding
chapters.intro: The original taxonomy predates today's async, distributed, data-heavy, and heavily tested systems. These additions catch failure modes that senior engineers now encounter routinely.

concepts.title: Flag Arguments and Boolean Blindness
concepts.definition: Flag Arguments and Boolean Blindness occur when a true/false parameter selects between distinct behaviors but the call site does not reveal which behavior was requested.
concepts.look_for: Look for calls such as `Publish(post, true)` that require opening the method or reading a comment. Replace the selector with explicit methods or a meaningful enum.
concepts.python_expanded:
# Before: True does not reveal the requested behavior.
publish(post, True)


# After: each intention has a name.
def publish_draft(post):
    publish(post, mode="draft")


def publish_live(post):
    publish(post, mode="live")


publish_live(post)
concepts.walkthrough: At the original call site, `true` carries no domain vocabulary. A reader must inspect `Publish` to learn whether it means live, validated, immediate, public, or something else. `PublishLive` makes the caller's intention explicit, while `PublishMode` gives internal dispatch a named set of choices. If draft and live paths grow independently, the explicit methods can later own separate behavior. Python keyword arguments improve the compact call - `publish(post, live=True)` - but an enum or separate function may still be clearer when the flag selects two workflows. This smell applies to behavior selectors, not ordinary Boolean data. `customer.IsActive` is meaningful state, and `SetEnabled(bool enabled)` may be an honest setter. The pressure appears when `true` and `false` effectively stand for commands with different intentions.
concepts.caution: Do not ban booleans as data. The smell is an opaque selector for distinct behavior, especially when literal values appear at call sites.
concepts.related: Related: Replace Parameter with Explicit Methods; Introduce Parameter Object; Boolean blindness

concepts.title: Hidden Global State
concepts.definition: Hidden Global State is mutable process-wide or ambient data that influences behavior without appearing in a signature or declared dependency. Tests become order-dependent and concurrency becomes hazardous.
concepts.look_for: Look for writable statics, singletons, ambient request context, and module variables read deep inside business logic. Pass the value or capability explicitly.
concepts.walkthrough: The earlier design depended on `GlobalClock.Current`, but neither the constructor nor `IsExpired` revealed that dependency. A test changing the global clock could affect another test, and parallel work could observe timing-dependent state. `TokenService` now receives `IClock` explicitly and uses its local `clock` field. The caller controls which clock participates, tests can inject a fixed value, and the dependency graph becomes visible. Python removes the equivalent module-level variable in favor of constructor injection. Global immutable constants do not create the same problem because readers do not need mutation history to predict them. Ambient state can still be justified at carefully bounded infrastructure layers, such as a request context, but allowing domain code to reach it freely makes behavior hard to reproduce. Dependency injection is the shown remedy; the smell is the invisible, mutable influence.
concepts.caution: Truly immutable constants are different from hidden mutable state. Do not replace simple constants with injected services merely to eliminate all global names.
concepts.related: Related: Dependency injection; Mutable Shared State; Referential transparency

concepts.title: Mutable Shared State
concepts.definition: Mutable Shared State exists when multiple threads, tasks, callbacks, or modules can read and write the same value. Correctness then depends on access timing and ownership rules that may be invisible.
concepts.look_for: Look for shared collections, counters, caches, and singleton state changed from multiple execution paths. Prefer one owner, immutable messages, or one narrow synchronized operation.
concepts.walkthrough: A plain `value++` is a read-modify-write sequence: two threads can read the same old value and lose one increment. `Counter.Increment` narrows mutation to `Interlocked.Increment`, and `Read` uses `Volatile.Read` so the memory access policy is explicit. Every access must follow that discipline. The Python example demonstrates a stronger ownership approach: producers place immutable increment requests on a `Queue`, while one `CounterOwner` applies updates to `_value`. Python's GIL is not a general guarantee that compound operations or cross-process state are safe; explicit ownership remains useful. Locks and atomics address data races, but they do not automatically establish higher-level correctness. If several fields must change as one invariant, protecting each field separately is insufficient. Prefer designs that reduce the number of writers and make the mutation boundary obvious.
concepts.caution: A lock or atomic operation helps only when every relevant access follows the same protocol and the protected scope matches the invariant. One clear owner is often easier to verify.
concepts.related: Related: Immutability; Race Condition; Actor model; Concurrency

concepts.title: Temporal Coupling
concepts.definition: Temporal Coupling requires API calls to occur in a particular order even though the type and method names do not make that sequence safe or obvious.
concepts.look_for: Look for `Initialize`-before-`Use`, setters required before `Build`, or methods that fail only because another method was not called first. Construct valid state atomically or model lifecycle states.
concepts.walkthrough: The problematic API allowed a `Document` to exist before its text was loaded or parsed, so callers had to remember a hidden sequence. `Document.Parse` now performs parsing and construction together and the private C# constructor prevents an unparsed instance. Once a `Document` exists, `Lines` is valid. Python cannot enforce constructor privacy in the same way, but the `parse` class method communicates the intended creation path and can be paired with conventions or validation. Some domains are inherently sequential - network connections, transactions, and media players have real states. In those cases the remedy is not to pretend sequence disappeared, but to expose a state machine or separate types for each phase. Temporal Coupling is about an undocumented or unenforced order that makes ordinary misuse easy.
concepts.caution: Some protocols genuinely require sequence. Represent that lifecycle explicitly with state, types, or guarded transitions instead of hiding it behind undocumented call order.
concepts.related: Related: Replace Constructor with Factory Method; State; Typestate

concepts.title: Leaky Abstraction
concepts.definition: A Leaky Abstraction exposes implementation details that its callers should not need, such as SQL, HTTP headers, vendor exceptions, or storage layout. Consumers become coupled to the hidden detail anyway.
concepts.look_for: When application code catches vendor exceptions or assembles database syntax through a supposed domain interface, translate operations and failures at the boundary.
concepts.walkthrough: `ICustomerRepository` speaks in application terms: find a `Customer` by `EmailAddress`. `SqlCustomerRepository` owns SQL execution and translates `SqlException` into `CustomerStoreUnavailable`. The caller no longer knows table names, parameter syntax, or the selected database driver. If the adapter instead returned data readers or required callers to catch `SqlException`, the repository name would hide little; the abstraction would leak. Python performs the same translation at the repository boundary. No abstraction can conceal every property of its implementation - latency, transaction semantics, and consistency may be relevant to correct use. The goal is to hide volatile or irrelevant detail while documenting unavoidable constraints. Escape hatches can be legitimate when named explicitly rather than smuggled through the main interface.
concepts.caution: Every abstraction leaks under some pressure. Hide volatile and irrelevant detail, document operational semantics that affect correctness, and provide deliberate escape hatches when necessary.
concepts.related: Related: Adapter; Dependency Inversion Principle; Exception translation

concepts.title: Dependency Cycles
concepts.definition: A Dependency Cycle exists when modules depend on one another directly or through a loop. No member of the cycle can be understood, tested, built, or deployed independently of the others.
concepts.look_for: Use dependency graphs and build references to find loops. Move a shared contract toward the stable policy or into a neutral module that both sides can depend on.
concepts.walkthrough: Suppose Billing called Shipping directly while Shipping imported a Billing model to inspect payment state. That creates a cycle in source dependencies and business ownership. Moving the neutral `OrderPaid` contract outside both modules lets Billing publish a fact and Shipping consume it without importing Billing's internals. The dependency graph now points from both components toward the contract rather than around a loop. An event is not the only remedy; sometimes one module clearly owns the interface, or shared behavior belongs in a third cohesive component. A mediator can make calls indirect while preserving the conceptual cycle, so check ownership rather than only whether build tooling reports a loop. Python imports are especially prone to runtime circular-import failures, but the deeper cost is entangled reasoning and change. Events also introduce delivery and consistency concerns that must be handled elsewhere.
concepts.caution: Do not declare a cycle solved merely because a mediator hides direct calls. Verify that business ownership and source dependencies now point in an intentional acyclic direction.
concepts.related: Related: Dependency Inversion Principle; Acyclic Dependencies Principle; Mediator

concepts.title: Sync-over-Async
concepts.definition: Sync-over-Async blocks a thread while waiting for an asynchronous operation, commonly through `.Result`, `.Wait()`, or equivalent bridges. It wastes capacity and can deadlock under a synchronization context.
concepts.look_for: When an operation awaits I/O, propagate `async` and cancellation through its callers instead of converting the task back into a synchronous wait.
concepts.python_expanded:
# Before: a synchronous wrapper drove the event loop itself.
async def load_customer(customer_id, client):
    response = await client.get(f"customers/{customer_id}")
    response.raise_for_status()
    customer = response.json()
    if customer is None:
        raise CustomerNotFound(customer_id)
    return customer
concepts.walkthrough: The corrected C# method returns `Task<Customer>` and awaits the HTTP call. While the response is pending, the thread is available for other work. `CancellationToken` remains visible so abandonment can travel to the network boundary. Calling `.Result` or `.Wait()` would block and, in UI or older request contexts, might wait for a continuation that is itself trying to resume on the blocked context. Python has the same boundary problem when synchronous code calls `asyncio.run` from an active loop or otherwise blocks the event-loop thread. The remedy is 'async all the way' through the relevant call chain. Async improves utilization for waiting; it does not make CPU-bound work intrinsically faster. Such work may need parallel execution, batching, or a worker process instead.
concepts.caution: Do not treat async as automatic speed. It improves how waiting resources are used; CPU-bound work needs a separate performance and concurrency decision.
concepts.related: Related: Async programming; Cancellation; Deadlock

concepts.title: Chatty I/O and N+1 Queries
concepts.definition: Chatty I/O and N+1 Queries perform one remote or database operation per item after an initial query. Latency and load grow with record count rather than useful work.
concepts.look_for: Inspect loops containing repository, HTTP, or filesystem calls. Fetch a set, join at the source, prefetch relationships, or process bounded batches.
concepts.python_expanded:
# Before: get_customer ran once for every order.
customer_ids = set()
for order in orders:
    customer_ids.add(order.customer_id)

customers = await repository.get_many(customer_ids)

for order in orders:
    customer = customers[order.customer_id]
    print_order(order, customer)
concepts.walkthrough: The N+1 version first loads `orders` and then calls the repository once per order to obtain its customer. Twenty orders produce twenty-one round trips; a thousand orders produce a thousand and one. The revised code collects distinct `customerIds`, performs one set-oriented `GetManyAsync`, and uses the returned dictionary locally. Network latency and connection overhead are paid once for the batch rather than once per record. The C# expanded version deliberately uses loops so the operation count is visible; LINQ can compact ID selection but does not change the cost model. Python follows the same set-and-map approach. A single enormous batch can exceed parameter limits, produce poor query plans, or consume too much memory, so production code may use measured chunk sizes. Detect this smell with query logs, traces, round-trip counts, and realistic data volumes rather than source aesthetics alone.
concepts.caution: Batching has limits. Measure query plans, payload size, memory, and latency, then choose joins, prefetching, or bounded batches appropriate to the data source.
concepts.related: Related: Performance engineering; DataLoader; Eager loading

concepts.title: Catch-All Exception Handling
concepts.definition: Catch-All Exception Handling treats unrelated failures as one recoverable condition, often erasing diagnostics, retrying unsafe work, or pretending an operation succeeded.
concepts.look_for: Catch an exception only when the current layer can recover, add meaningful context, translate it for its caller, or perform a safe compensating action.
concepts.walkthrough: The previous broad catch would have converted timeouts, programming defects, cancellation, and data corruption into the same `null` or `None` result. The revised code catches only `TimeoutException` or `TimeoutError`, adds the customer identifier, and preserves the original exception as the cause. Callers can now distinguish an unavailable store from a missing customer or a bug. Other failures continue to a boundary equipped to log and produce a safe response. Broad catches are legitimate at process, job, or request boundaries where the system must contain unexpected failure, but even there the cause should be recorded and success must not be fabricated. Retry decisions also belong to known transient failures and idempotent operations, not to every exception. C# cancellation exceptions usually deserve propagation, and Python's cancellation behavior likewise requires care.
concepts.caution: Top-level boundaries should contain unexpected exceptions, but they must preserve diagnostics and return an honest failure. Never retry or suppress all exceptions indiscriminately.
concepts.related: Related: Exception translation; Retry; Result type; Observability

concepts.title: Anemic Domain Model
concepts.definition: An Anemic Domain Model stores domain state in passive objects while services own all invariants and transitions. Rules scatter, and callers can bypass them by mutating fields directly.
concepts.look_for: When several services manipulate the same entity fields to enforce one stable business rule, move that rule to the entity or value object that owns the invariant.
concepts.walkthrough: `Account.Withdraw` owns the invariant that a withdrawal must be positive and cannot exceed `Balance`. Callers request the transition instead of calculating a new balance and assigning it. That prevents one service from forgetting the rule and gives the domain vocabulary a concrete home. An application service may still coordinate authentication, transactions, persistence, and notifications around the withdrawal; those effects do not belong inside the entity merely to make it 'rich.' Python uses `_balance` and a read-only property by convention to direct changes through `withdraw`. Anemic models are most costly in rule-heavy domains with meaningful invariants and lifecycles. A CRUD application whose records truly carry little behavior may be clearer with data-centric models and explicit services. The smell is procedural scattering of real domain knowledge, not the existence of DTOs.
concepts.caution: Do not force behavior into entities when the application is genuinely data-centric or the operation coordinates external systems. Richness should follow real domain rules.
concepts.related: Related: Data Class; Encapsulation; Domain-Driven Design

concepts.title: Distributed Monolith
concepts.definition: A Distributed Monolith consists of separately deployed services that must still change, release, or remain available together because they share persistence, internal models, or synchronous call chains.
concepts.look_for: Look for coordinated releases, cross-service database writes, lockstep versioning, and one user request that fails when any service in a long chain is unavailable.
concepts.walkthrough: `OrderAccepted` is a stable fact published by the Orders service. Billing consumes only the order identifier and total, then owns invoice creation. It does not read Orders' tables or import its internal entity classes. This boundary allows the two services to deploy and fail more independently than a synchronous chain over shared persistence. The example does not prove an architecture is no longer a distributed monolith; team ownership, release practice, contracts, and operational dependencies must agree. Events also replace immediate consistency with delivery concerns: messages can be late, duplicated, or processed out of order, so Billing needs idempotency and monitoring. A modular monolith often provides clearer boundaries with far less operational cost when independent deployment is not yet required. Python's handler expresses the same ownership and asynchronous integration.
concepts.caution: Do not split a healthy modular monolith merely to avoid the label. Events add delivery, consistency, debugging, and operational costs that must be justified by independent change or scale.
concepts.related: Related: Modular Monolith; Service boundaries; Event-Driven Architecture

concepts.title: Test Smells
concepts.definition: Test Smells are recurring test structures that reduce trust or increase maintenance: flakiness, excessive setup, over-mocking, order dependence, slow feedback, and assertions tied to private implementation.
concepts.look_for: Prefer deterministic inputs and assertions on observable behavior at the narrowest realistic boundary. Investigate tests that fail intermittently or break after behavior-preserving refactoring.
concepts.python_expanded:
def test_total_sums_line_amounts():
    lines = [OrderLine(4), OrderLine(6)]
    order = Order(lines)

    result = order.calculate_total()

    assert result == 10
concepts.walkthrough: The test constructs an order from two line amounts, calls the public `CalculateTotal` behavior, and asserts the result. It does not mock the list, assert which private helper ran, depend on clock time, or require another test to execute first. A refactoring that changes internal iteration while preserving the total should leave this test green. That makes the test an asset rather than a brake on design. A test double is not inherently a smell; replacing a payment gateway or clock at a stable boundary can make a focused test reliable. Trouble begins when mocks reenact every internal call and therefore encode the implementation twice. Likewise, integration tests are not bad because they are slower; their scope should justify their feedback cost. C# and Python versions protect the same observable contract through their customary test styles.
concepts.caution: Do not respond to every smell by deleting coverage or banning mocks. Match the test level and double to a real boundary, and preserve confidence in behavior.
concepts.related: Related: Testing pyramid; Characterization Test; Test Double
